definitions.meaning: The distance covered in one unit of time: a speed of 60 km/h means the bus covers 60 km in every hour.
An amount per unit of something else: speed is a rate, the distance travelled per hour.
How far something travels, found by multiplying speed by time: at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours the distance is 150 km.
How long a journey lasts: the time together with the speed decides the distance, so half an hour gives half the distance of a full hour.

mechanismSteps: Speed is distance per hour: a bus at 60 km/h covers 60 km in one hour, 120 km in two hours and 180 km in three hours - the same 60 km landing every hour.
60 km/h for 2.5 hours: distance = speed × time, so 60 × 2.5 = 150 km - 60 km in each full hour plus 30 km in the half hour.
Watch out: speed is not distance: 60 km/h names a rate, not a total - after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, because half the time means half the distance.
The takeaway: distance = speed × time, and the formula flips either way - speed = distance ÷ time and time = distance ÷ speed.
objectives: Read a speed as a rate: 60 km/h as 60 km covered in every hour
Find a distance by multiplying speed by time, and flip the formula to find a speed or a time

trap.explanation: A rate is read as a total instead of an amount per unit of time. Speed is distance per hour: after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, not 60. In the animation scene s3 the claim is tested against the road and fails: after half an hour the bus sits at the 30 km mark, not the 60 km mark.
trap.misconception: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km.

workedExample: In scene s2, a bus travelling at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours is worked with distance = speed × time: 60 × 2.5 = 150 km. Step by step: 60 km in the first hour, 60 km in the second hour, and 30 km in the final half hour, and the parts check: 60 + 60 + 30 = 150 km.
